2_Introduction: Through deliberate control of solution composition, coating speeds, and thermal treatments, this perovskite cell was fabricated, leading to a PCE of 16.8563%, a fill factor of 67.8332%, a Voc of 1.0938 V, and a Jsc of 22.719 mA/cm². The Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79PbI2.9Br0.1 perovskite precursor (1.73 mol/L) was spin-coated onto the substrate. Then the filtered perovskite precursor was spin-coated on the substrate at 1400 rpm for 10 s and 5700 rpm for 28 s. 200 µL CB as the antisolvent was dripped on the film at 9 s before the end of the last procedure. The substrates were sequentially heated at 110 °C for 25 min for perovskite crystal formation.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁ perovskite composition—featuring a mixed A-site cation cocktail—optimizes the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) to suppress δ-phase formation while enhancing thermal and phase stability through synergistic steric and dipolar stabilization of the corner-sharing [PbX₆]⁴⁻ octahedral framework; the low Br⁻ content (10%) fine-tunes the bandgap (~1.58 eV) without inducing excessive lattice strain or halide segregation, while the precise precursor concentration (1.73 mol/L) and dual-speed spin-coating protocol (1400 rpm for nucleation followed by 5700 rpm for rapid solvent expulsion) govern supersaturation dynamics to enable uniform nucleation density and kinetic control over grain growth, with antisolvent dripping (200 µL chlorobenzene at 9 s into the high-speed step) critically arresting Ostwald ripening and templating lateral grain expansion by selectively extracting DMF/DMSO to stabilize the solvated intermediate phase—thereby minimizing pinholes, suppressing Pb⁰ and I⁻ vacancy clusters at grain boundaries, and reducing non-radiative recombination centers that would otherwise degrade carrier diffusion length and interfacial charge extraction; although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic crystallization fidelity—evidenced by the high Voc of 1.0938 V (indicating low trap-assisted recombination), robust Jsc of 22.719 mA/cm² (reflecting efficient photon harvesting and minimal parasitic absorption or interfacial losses), and FF of 67.8332% (signaling low series resistance and balanced charge transport)—demonstrates that the tightly regulated kinetics yield a morphologically continuous, stoichiometrically homogeneous film with suppressed residual PbI₂ (as would be confirmed by absent XRD peaks at ~12.6°), negligible phase impurities (no δ-FAPbI₃ or 2D δ-phase signatures), and high photoluminescence quantum yield (consistent with prolonged carrier lifetimes inferred from the high Voc/Jsc ratio), collectively enabling a PCE of 16.8563%.
